Summary: Query Contract: select subject and objective from the full submitted context, lock them, then resolve and analyze
Description: 1) Original intent: KRYLO must determine what the user is asking about (subject) and what they want to know about it (objective) before entity resolution or structural analysis begins, producing one authoritative Query Contract. Core invariant from the draft spec: SUBJECT + OBJECTIVE ARE THE QUERY CONTRACT; ordering SELECT -> LOCK -> RESOLVE -> ANALYZE. Source: specs/Query Contract -- Summary Specification.md (Founder-authored, DRAFT v2, 2026-10-07; section 2 Class E, actual capability gap). 2) Acceptance criteria: one QueryContract (subject text, canonicalId or null, attribution RESOLVED / UNRESOLVED / AMBIGUOUS / NONE; objective; mentions with roles) is built from the complete submitted analysis context before resolution, locked, and consumed by every downstream surface (brief, left column, MAP, domain tabs). Must cover: (a) implicit subjects supplied by the target content; (b) short decision questions such as 'Good investment?', 'Good merger?', 'Good deal?'; (c) transaction or combined-entity subjects such as Paramount / WBD; (d) the subject is retained, with attribution UNRESOLVED, when canonical resolution subsequently fails; (e) objective is selected independently of subject resolution; (f) contextual entities such as Netflix do not displace the subject; (g) comparison of competing subjects yields AMBIGUOUS; (h) no subject yields NONE, never a guess. Regression fixtures: Daytona question resolving to META PLATFORMS (wrong subject), Subcritical Systems question resolving to SPACEX (wrong subject), and a Paramount / WBD deal question. A test matrix by input class (explicit subject, implicit this, single entity, multiple entities, comparison, unresolved subject, no subject, investment / acquisition / structural questions, subject plus objective reaching every downstream surface) is run against the pure selector. 3) Current implementation state: not built. Subject resolution today is spread across subjectscope.js, structuralqueryinterpreter.js and querysynthesis.js, and long thematic queries have been observed collapsing onto large ambient entities (META PLATFORMS, SPACEX). No analysis API exists; analysis runs in the browser (synthesizeQuery called from React components), so validation outside the app needs the selector to be a pure function runnable in Node. 4) Dependencies and OPEN items that block build under section 10: (a) the draft spec file in the repository is truncated at 1,450 bytes (ends inside section 2) and must be re-saved in full (sections 1-13 and Appendix A); (b) the objective taxonomy has no explicit value for deal or merger evaluation and must be settled in the spec before implementation (not forced into an existing category by inference); (c) Founder authorization for build (spec marked not authorized for build); (d) line references in Appendix A were traced against 343d104 and must be rechecked against current main. Related: KRYL-1359, KRYL-1360, specs/def-subject-resolution-admits-subject-not-in-query-20261006.md (unfiled defect draft this ticket supersedes if accepted). 5) Superseded by a newer ticket: none known; it supersedes the unfiled subject-resolution defect draft. 6) Maps to current product model: yes; selects what is being asked before analysis and presents structure without drawing the guest's conclusion (sections 17 and 21).
